bullets: Described as ‘all in a glow; his face was ruddy and handsome; his eyes sparkled’: **warmth imagery** contrasts with Scrooge’s cold.

His speech defending Christmas: ‘a good time; a kind, forgiving, charitable, pleasant time… when men and women seem by one consent to open their shut-up hearts freely, and to think of people below them as if they really were fellow-passengers to the grave, and not another race of creatures bound on other journeys.’
The **list of adjectives** sums up Dickens’s Christmas values; ‘fellow-passengers to the grave’ argues for **equality**: everyone shares death.
He admits Christmas has never put money in his pocket but has done him good: values above money.
Bob applauds the speech: the poor recognise its truth.
He refuses to quarrel: ‘I’ll keep my Christmas humour to the last.’
core.p: Fred visits Scrooge’s counting-house to invite him to Christmas dinner.

bullets: Fred laughs warmly and says he pities Scrooge: ‘His offences carry their own punishment’; ‘Who suffers by his ill whims? Himself, always.’
He intends to invite Scrooge every year: **persistence** of kindness.
Party games (Yes and No, Blind Man’s Buff): joy, community; Scrooge wants to join.
core.p: The Ghost of Christmas Present shows Fred’s party.

bullets: ‘Let him in! It is a mercy he didn’t shake his arm off.’ Fred welcomes him instantly.
‘Wonderful party, wonderful games, wonderful unanimity, wonderful happiness!’: repetition of ‘wonderful’: complete reconciliation.
core.p: Scrooge visits Fred’s house, unsure of his welcome.

bullets: **Foil** to Scrooge: young, warm, poor-ish but happy vs old, cold, rich and miserable.
Link to the past: son of Scrooge’s beloved sister **Fan**; rejecting Fred means rejecting her memory.
Mouthpiece for Dickens’s view of Christmas.
Shows the power of **forgiveness and persistence**.

callouts.p: Fred’s marriage was for love, not money; Scrooge mocks this in Stave 1. It recalls Belle and the love Scrooge chose to give up.

exam.q: Explain how Dickens presents Fred elsewhere in the novella. (20 marks)
exam.tip: Explain Fred’s function, not just his personality.

mistakes.r: He wants nothing; he admits Christmas never put money in his pocket.

quotes.a: Equality of all people; social responsibility.

quotes.q: a kind, forgiving, charitable, pleasant time

quotes.a: Pity, not anger; Scrooge harms himself.
quotes.q: His offences carry their own punishment

summary: Fred, Scrooge’s nephew, is the voice of the Christmas spirit: cheerful, generous and persistent, he never gives up on his uncle; he is Scrooge’s foil and Dickens’s model of how to keep Christmas.

terms.d: A character who contrasts with another, highlighting their qualities.
A character who voices the author’s views.
